definition_used: When a journal/publisher/institution states that one or more authors have not met the journal/publisher/institution’s standards of publishing and/or research ethics. RW will use this reason when no other information about the correction/EOC/retraction is available (i.e., the notice only states that there was an ethical violation), or when the ethical violation (as an additional reason) cannot be addressed by existing reasons.
caution: The definition is broad and often used as a catch-all when specifics are unavailable. Without further details, the exact nature of the ethical violation is ambiguous, but it inherently involves author conduct and journal/institutional standards.
semantic_rationale: The reason indicates a breach of publishing/research ethics by authors, as determined by a journal, publisher, or institution. This directly implicates author integrity (attribution_authorship_disclosure_integrity) and the governance of ethical standards (editorial_peer_review_governance). The problem object is set to article_general due to lack of specificity. Process signals reflect investigation and policy enforcement by the journal/publisher/institution.
